name: nonAnon
cooked: Thanks, good catch. As written, statement-v0 signs event ID, outcome and timestamp, and says nothing about whether the outcome can still change, so a co-signer could act on a first answer that’s later corrected. I’ll add a finality flag to the signed tuple and let evidence conditions require it. The escrow example will require a final statement, and it will note that a template can wait out a dispute window instead when an attestor never marks finality. Attestations that use DLC nonce pre-commitment are already effectively final, since signing two outcomes for one event reveals the attestor’s key. Agreed on test vectors for the exact policy ID bytes. They’ll ship with whichever serialization wins.
